items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: All the acts – Odetta, Miriam Makeba – were assembled on the stage, and the musicians.

ctx.x: . . . energy, I would dash this thing off, and everybody would say, oh, it’s great. In fact, at Monterey, when I did the first production of Evolution of the Blues, John Lewis was musical director. Jimmy Lyons was on stage making the announcement about this world premiere performance that they were going to have. All the acts – Odetta, Miriam Makeba – were assembled on the stage, and the musicians. I was walking up the steps writing on my pad. John Lewis was a nervous wreck. He said, “You mean, you’re not…

That’s remarkable. I’ve seen you do that at least a couple of times. I just thought that it was amazing for you to walk up on a stage and pull out a sheet of paper and just began singing this very difficult song and hitting every note and just doing it perfectly, for me. I think that’s . . .
